scenarios.name: clean_coil_holding_setpoint
scenarios.description: NO_FAULT: the loop sits at 45% against a fitted 42% and holds supply air 0.2 K off a 13.0 °C setpoint. Three points of hydraulic excess is fit residual, not fouling, and yInControlOk is true the whole run so the silence means healthy rather than unevaluated.

scenarios.name: fouled_coil_alarms_at_the_persistence_edge
scenarios.description: FAULT, and the whole point of the card: supply air is still 0.2 K off setpoint — thermally the unit looks perfect — while the valve holds 65% where the fit expects 42%. The alarm lands at exactly 3600 s, which also pins delayOnInit: the condition is present from the first tick and still serves the full hour.

scenarios.name: excess_exactly_at_the_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary, bit-exact: 52.0 − 42.0 is exactly 10.0 and the parameter is exactly 10.0, so the verdict is decided by the strictness of Reals.GreaterThreshold and not by rounding. A valve sitting exactly on the creep line reads healthy.

scenarios.name: excess_just_above_the_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary from above: one hundredth of a percent more valve opening puts the excess at 10.01 points and the rule alarms on the normal schedule.

scenarios.name: in_control_band_exactly_at_the_edge_is_no_eval
scenarios.description: NO_EVAL boundary: 14.0 − 13.0 is exactly 1.0 and Reals.LessThreshold is strict, so a loop sitting exactly on the band edge is NOT in control. The hydraulic excess is 23 points and the rule still says nothing — yInControlOk false is the only thing that distinguishes this from a clean coil.

scenarios.name: in_control_band_just_inside_alarms
scenarios.description: The other side of the same boundary: 13.99 against 13.0 is 0.99 K of tracking error, inside the band, and the same 23 points of excess now count. Together with the previous scenario this pins both sides of the evaluability gate.

scenarios.name: loop_lost_control_is_no_eval
scenarios.description: NO_EVAL: the valve is pinned at 100% and supply air runs 4 K warm. This is a coil that has stopped meeting its setpoint, which is AHU-0033's finding and a louder one; the excess-over-baseline arithmetic means nothing once the loop is saturated, so this card stands down.

scenarios.name: overcooling_side_of_the_band_is_no_eval
scenarios.description: NO_EVAL on the cold side, and the vector that pins the Abs: sat − sat_sp is −1.5 K, which is less than the 1.0 K band as a signed number and outside it as a magnitude. Without absErr the rule would read an overcooling loop as in control and count its open valve as fouling.

scenarios.name: fan_off_signature_is_absent
scenarios.description: Why the fan gate is a host precondition rather than a conjunct in the graph: with the fan stopped the cooling valve is driven shut, so the excess is −45 points and the fault term is false on arithmetic alone. Nothing charges the persistence timer overnight, which is the failure mode that put the fan status inside AHU-0036's graph.

scenarios.name: loop_excursion_restarts_persistence
scenarios.description: A single tick outside the control band at 1800 s — a load step the loop has to chase — drops the evaluability gate and restarts the hour. The alarm moves from 3600 s to 5460 s, one delay after the loop settles back inside the band.

scenarios.name: excess_dip_restarts_persistence
scenarios.description: The same restart driven from the other conjunct: the valve backs off to 50% for one tick, putting the excess at 8 points, then returns to 65%. The creep gate cycles off and on and the alarm lands at 5460 s.

scenarios.name: coil_cleaned_mid_run_clears_the_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 3600 s, then the coil is washed at 4800 s and the same duty is met at 44% — two points of excess. TrueDelay drops on the falling edge with no release delay, so the fault clears on the tick the valve backs off.

scenarios.name: baseline_fitted_on_a_fouled_coil_stays_silent
scenarios.description: The point dictionary's known-clean caveat made executable. The valve is at 65% and the coil is fouled, but the host fitted the baseline from that same period and publishes 64%, so the excess is one point and the rule is quiet forever. Nothing in the graph can see this; the fit window is a commissioning obligation.
